meta.name: CBL-16 Dynamic Risk Adjustment Layer
meta.purpose: Literature-informed, expert-adjustable multipliers applied on top of the static LSOA risk index to produce a current-conditions risk score.
meta.contract: The dashboard consumes this config plus per-LSOA static inputs. For a given date/time it (1) reads the day's feature values, (2) computes each active factor's literature-default multiplier, (3) lets the officer override the multiplier within [min,max], (4) applies the formula below. The static index is never modified.
meta.important: All effect sizes are ILLUSTRATIVE LITERATURE-INFORMED DEFAULTS, not values estimated from the project's own crime data (police.uk street crime is month-level only and has no time-of-day, so weekend/night/holiday/match effects cannot be derived locally). Treat them as priors the officer updates.

formula.active: a factor contributes only when its applies_when condition is true; otherwise its multiplier = 1.0

global_caps.note: Prevents a stack of factors (or aggressive overrides) from producing an absurd score.

per_day_global.name: temp_c
per_day_global.source: extend existing NetCDF to daily, or live forecast API (e.g. Met Office / Open-Meteo)

per_lsoa_static.name: bar_count
per_lsoa_static.desc: count of on-licence premises (pubs/bars/clubs) in the LSOA

per_lsoa_static.name: bar_density_norm
per_lsoa_static.desc: bar_count normalised to [0,1] across London (or per km2)

per_lsoa_static.name: stadium_proximity_flag
per_lsoa_static.desc: 1 if LSOA is within the catchment of a football stadium
per_lsoa_static.source: stadium coords + buffer / LSOA boundary join

per_day_event.name: match_day
per_day_event.desc: 1 if a home fixture is played that day at the linked stadium

per_day_event.name: match_band
per_day_event.desc: low | medium | high (by attendance / derby / cup)

factors.label: Temperature
factors.rationale: Positive temperature-violence relationship in temperate climates. ~1.2% uplift in violent/public-order crime per degree C above a mild reference; suppressed in cold weather (fewer people outdoors).

factors.label: Cloud cover / poor weather
factors.rationale: Proxy for precipitation/poor weather, which tends to suppress outdoor and property crime via routine-activity (fewer targets/people outside). Evidence weaker than temperature - keep small range and flag as low confidence. Consider replacing with a direct precipitation input.

factors.label: Weekend
factors.rationale: Violent and public-order crime concentrate on weekends, driven largely by the night-time economy. Saturday highest.

factors.label: Public / bank holiday
factors.rationale: Heterogeneous effect: alcohol-related violence and public-order tend to rise (esp. festive period / NYE), while commercial property crime can fall when businesses close. Net uplift modest; flag NYE as a special high case in the dashboard.

factors.label: Fri/Sat night x bar density
factors.applies_when: day_of_week in [Fri, Sat] AND is_night == true

model.note: bar_density_norm in [0,1]; LSOA with no bars -> multiplier 1.0; densest nightlife LSOA -> up to 1.40

factors.rationale: On-premise alcohol outlet density is one of the better-evidenced spatial correlates of assault and public-order offences, concentrated on Friday/Saturday nights. Effect scales with local outlet density.

factors.label: Football match day (near stadium)
factors.rationale: Match days raise property crime and violence in the area immediately around stadia; effect is spatially localised and scales with attendance / rivalry. Note also documented rises in domestic abuse linked to England match outcomes - consider as a separate force-wide flag.
